FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Cutting 
Tools Sectional Committee had been approved by the Production and General Engineering Division Council. 


This standard has been formulated based on the prevalent practice followed by the Indian industry. In formulating 
this standard considerable assistance has been derived from DIN 6539 : 1991 "Continuous parallel shank solid 
hard metal twist drills — Dimensions” and IS 5101 : 1991 "Twist drills, parallel shank, jobber series — Specification 
(first revision)’. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16059 : 2013 


Indian Standard 


SOLID CARBIDE PARALLEL SHANK TWIST DRILLS 
JOBBER SERIES — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard specifies dimensions and other 
requirements for solid carbide parallel shank twist 
drills, jobber series. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
listed below: 


IS No. Title 


919 (Part 2) : ISO system of limits and fits: Part 2 
1993 Tables of standard tolerance grades 
and limit deviations for holes and 
shafts (first revision) 
General tolerances: Part 1 Tolerances 
for linear and angular dimensions 
without individual tolerance indications 
(third revision) 
Classification and application of hard 
cutting materials for material removal 
with defined cutting edges — 
Designation of the main groups and 
groups of application (second revision) 


2102 (Part 1) : 
1993 


2428 : 2007 


3 DIMENSIONS 


3.1 Dimensions shall be as given in Table I (see Fig. 1). 
Tolerances on diameters shall be as per IS 919 (Part 2). 


3.2 The back taper shall be provided on cutting portion 
of the drill. The value of back taper shall be 0.02 to 0.3 
mm/100 mm flute length. 


NOTE — Back taper is not obligatory for diameters less than 
3 mm but in no case shall the diameter at point be less than at 
the rest of fluted portion. 


4 MATERIAL 


The solid carbide shall be of chip removal group P or 
K (as specified in IS 2428), at the manufacturer's 
discretion or subject to agreement. In the later case, 
the symbol for the application group shall be indicated, 
when ordering. 


5 DESIGNATION 


Solid carbide parallel shank twist drill, jobber series 
with 8.00 mm diameter, and grade K40, conforming 
to this standard shall be designated as: 


Twist Drill 8.00 K40 IS 16059 


6 TOLERANCES 


6.1 Tolerance on overall length shall be “very coarse’ 
grade as given in IS 2102 (Part 1). 


6.2 The tolerance on radial run out shall be within 
0.02 mm. 


6.3 The tolerance on relative lip height shall be within 
0.03 mm. 


7 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS 


7.1 Unless otherwise specified right hand helix with 
right hand cutting shall be supplied. 


7.2 Unless otherwise specified, drills are provided with 
two flutes. 


8 MARKING 


8.1 Each drill of diameter 3 mm and above shall be 
marked with the following: 


a) Diameter; 
b) Grade of material; and 
c) Manufacturer's name or trade-mark. 


In case of drills below 3 mm diameter; the marking 
shall be done on the packing. 


8.1.1 The marking shall not affect the clamping or 
functioning of the drill. 


8.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


8.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the 
provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the license for the 
use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers 
or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of 
Indian Standards.

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


“BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: PGD 32 (0508).
